record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Let M be a k-polymatroid, meaning a polymatroid ρ: 2^E → Z with ρ(e) ≤ k for every element e of the ground set E. Is M hypergraphic; that is, does there exist a hypergraph H on edge set E such that M is the hypergraphic polymatroid χ_H defined by χ_H(A) = |A| − κ(H|A) for every A ⊆ E, where A is the set of vertices contained in the hyperedge set A and κ(H|A) is the number of connected components of the restriction of H to A?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polymatroid on a finite ground set $E$ is a function $\rho:2^E\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ that is normalized ($\rho(\emptyset)=0$), monotone ($\rho(A)\le\rho(B)$ whenever $A\subseteq B\subseteq E$), and submodular ($\rho(A\cup B)+\rho(A\cap B)\le\rho(A)+\rho(B)$ for all $A,B\subseteq E$). For a positive integer $k$, a $k$-polymatroid is a polymatroid satisfying $\rho(\{e\})\le k$ for every $e\in E$.

Given a hypergraph $H=(V,E)$ with vertex set $V$ and (hyper)edge set $E$, the hypergraphic polymatroid of $H$ is the function $\chi_H:2^E\to\mathbb{Z}$ defined by
$$\chi_H(A)=|\widetilde A|-\kappa(H|A),\qquad A\subseteq E,$$
where $\widetilde A$ is the set of vertices incident to at least one hyperedge of $A$, $H|A=(\widetilde A,A)$ is the restriction of $H$ to $A$, and $\kappa(H|A)$ denotes the number of connected components of $H|A$. A polymatroid $M$ on ground set $E$ is called hypergraphic if $M=\chi_H$ for some hypergraph $H$ on edge set $E$.

Problem. Determine the parameterized complexity of the following decision problem, with parameter $k$:

Input: a positive integer $k$ and a $k$-polymatroid $M$ on a finite ground set $E$ (presented, e.g., by a rank oracle).
Parameter: $k$.
Question: Is $M$ hypergraphic?

Specifically, decide whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable in $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: Csirmaz, Matúš and Whittle ("Recognizing Polymatroids Associated with Hypergraphs", Combinatorics, Probability and Computing) give, for fixed k, a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether a k-polymatroid presented by a rank oracle is the hypergraphic polymatroid of some hypergraph (and finds one). This positively answers the recognition question in a strong sense for the rank-oracle model and is closely related to (and implies) FPT-style tractability. The exact formulation as posed in the parameterized-complexity list and any uniform FPT classification do not appear to be explicitly stated as completely settled in the parameterized literature.

status_evidence.title: Recognizing Polymatroids Associated with Hypergraphs
status_evidence.snippet: We give an algorithm that decides in polynomial time whether a k-polymatroid (given by a rank oracle) is the hypergraphic polymatroid associated with some hypergraph.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time recognition algorithm exists for hypergraphic k-polymatroids in the rank-oracle model.

status_evidence.title: Recognizing Polymatroids Associated with Hypergraphs (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Boolean and hypergraphic polymatroids associated with hypergraphs are recognized algorithmically.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic recognition of the hypergraphic polymatroid class is established.

status_evidence.title: On some algorithmic aspects of hypergraphic matroids
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms for graphic matroids extend to hypergraphic matroids, including independence testing and rank computation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent algorithmic work continues to develop the theory of hypergraphic (poly)matroids.
